chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Mamie Smith band personnel: Harvey Brooks, Joe Smith, Bob Fuller
summary: Players he recalls: pianist Harvey Brooks, trumpeter Joe Smith, violinist Henry Sapero, Cecil Carpenter and clarinetist Bob Fuller.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, played piano with you at that time?
Oh, (oh, unintelligible) fellow from -- from up in -- oh, (unintelligible) trumpet player. Trumpet player wasn't, but piano player was a (unintelligible) boy from out of Delaware.

And he had a group there too, but he wasn't with Mamie Smith when they first came to Chicago. The first one was this fellow that (unintelligible) boy of from Philadelphia name -- I think he still lives there too. Tall fellow, I can't call his name right off -- there, oh, Harvey Brooks.
Yeah, a good piano player, Harvey Brooks. Joe Smith on trumpet.
Joe Smith was on trumpet. We had a fellow named Henry Sappero (unintelligible) from St. Joe played violin (unintelligible) and doubled on banjo.
And then who was playing trumpet then when you were with them?
Oh, it was -- wasn't Joe (unintelligible) -- boy from out of Delaware too. There was the trumpet player with the piano player came up together around Wilmington, Delaware.
Sunny, oh -- he died too in -- they was very nice. We had Cecil Carpenter on trombone because Cecil was with the band when Hawk was there, and Bob Fuller Phillips
Oh, I see -- played nothing but

-- (unintelligible) clarinet, but John Chilton wrote to me about Bob Fuller and was he still living, where was he born and about Henry Supporo. Well, Supporo's a boy in New Orleans, and he had his own group around New York. I worked with him. Then we had the last group Lasko was Bamboo Inn in the band -- marine up on 7th Avenue, you know, and 140th Street. But Bob Fuller was with Mamie Smith when I first heard him, and they had -- they wanted me to join the band and wanted to get rid of Bob. But I wasn't ready for the band because I'm around here (unintelligible) born and doing good.
